subject: pathology
title: Skin pathology: blistering, papulosquamous disease and tumours

steps.tx: The level of the split separates the two great blistering diseases in exams. **Pemphigus vulgaris** splits within the epidermis above the basal layer and it causes flaccid bullae with oral erosions. Its antibodies attack desmogleins and immunofluorescence shows a **fishnet pattern** of IgG. **Bullous pemphigoid** splits below the epidermis and it causes tense bullae that usually spare the mouth in elderly patients.
steps.say: Pemphigus vulgaris causes flaccid blisters because the split lies within the epidermis. Patients often develop painful erosions inside the mouth. Bullous pemphigoid causes tense blisters because the split lies below the epidermis. The level of the split decides which disease the examiner describes.

steps.tx: **Dermatitis herpetiformis** causes intensely itchy grouped vesicles over extensor surfaces and it links with gluten sensitivity. Biopsy shows **granular IgA** deposited at the tips of dermal papillae, which is the diagnostic clue. The itch responds rapidly to dapsone while a gluten free diet controls the disease long term. Linear IgA disease differs because immunofluorescence shows a linear band and vancomycin is a recognised trigger.
steps.say: Dermatitis herpetiformis causes very itchy vesicles over the extensor surfaces. The biopsy is showing granular IgA at the tips of dermal papillae. Treatment with dapsone is relieving the itch within days. A gluten free diet controls the underlying disease over time.

steps.tx: **Psoriasis** shows parakeratosis with neutrophils collected as **Munro microabscesses** and regular thickening of the epidermis. Removing scale produces pinpoint bleeding called the Auspitz sign, and plaques favour elbows, knees, scalp and nails. Treatment steps from topical therapy and phototherapy toward systemic drugs and biologics in severe disease. Lichen planus differs with violaceous polygonal papules and white Wickham striae on the surface.
steps.say: Psoriasis produces silvery plaques over elbows, knees and the scalp. Removing the scale causes pinpoint bleeding from dilated capillaries below. Treatment is stepping from topical therapy toward systemic drugs and biologics. Lichen planus differs because its papules are violaceous and polygonal.

steps.tx: Three skin cancers dominate exam questions and each has a defining microscopic clue. **Basal cell carcinoma** grows slowly, rarely metastasises and shows nests with **peripheral palisading**. **Squamous cell carcinoma** forms keratin pearls and it can spread to regional nodes. Melanoma is staged by Breslow thickness and it needs wide excision with sentinel node assessment when indicated.
steps.say: Basal cell carcinoma grows slowly and it rarely spreads to distant sites. Squamous cell carcinoma forms keratin pearls and it can involve regional nodes. Melanoma is killing patients when clinicians are missing its early change. Breslow thickness stages melanoma and guides the width of excision.

steps.tx: This micrograph shows dark basaloid nests that belong to **basal cell carcinoma** in the dermis. The cells at the edge of each nest line up in a row called **peripheral palisading**, and a clear **stromal cleft** separates the nest from surrounding tissue. These two signs let the student name the tumour confidently. The tumour grows locally and it rarely metastasises despite its malignant name.
steps.say: This micrograph shows basaloid nests sitting within the dermis. The outer cells line up neatly and they show peripheral palisading. A clear cleft separates each nest from the surrounding stroma. These features identify basal cell carcinoma, which rarely metastasises.
